text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Taxi service reform planned by Public Transport Authority including opening a ticketing office at the airport for the payment of fixed fares, and a review of fares. Maltese taxis are seldom patronised by the Maltese because of their high fares. The taxi men also have a bad reputation for over- charging, particularly on tourist trips from the airport.

- Government plans to allocate special funds for Malta's south. Prime Minister Alfred Sant said on Sunday the government at its next budget at the end of the year intended to allocate special funds to improve public facilities in the south and reduce problems caused by industry. The south has the highest concentration of industry in Malta as well as the only airport, the freeport and the two power stations.

- Relatives of nine Malta Drydocks workers killed in an explosion on a Libyan tanker in February 1995 are still awaiting compensation from Malta Drydocks. A meeting with the new Malta Drydocks council is expected shortly.
